title: The Railroad Hour
paragraphs: Weekly musical-drama anthology sponsored by the Association of American Railroads, starring Gordon MacRae in condensed operettas, Broadway musicals and original musical stories.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: ABC 45-minute era (October 4, 1948 to April 18, 1949) on [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]], ABC 30-minute era (April 25, 1949 to September 26, 1949) on [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]], and NBC 30-minute era (October 3, 1949 to June 21, 1954) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Gordon MacRae (host, performer, and composer), Marvin Miller (announcer, performer, and narrator), Norman Luboff (performer, choir director, and conductor), Carmen Dragon (conductor, preparer, and composer), Robert E. Lee (radio adaptor, writer, and composer), Jerome Lawrence (radio adaptor, writer, and composer), and Dorothy Warenskjold (performer).

Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]], [[org|org.4798d1172deaae2c|Armed Forces Radio Service]], and [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]].

The stories often return to music, theater and performance, royalty, aristocracy and court society, travel and journeys, romance, courtship and marriage, war and military settings, and American historical and regional settings.
The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Postwar railroad-industry public relations, Broadway and operetta repertoire on network radio, and Late network-radio prestige programming.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]], [[show|the-whistler|The Whistler]], [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]], [[show|escape|Escape]], and [[show|screen-directors-playhouse|Screen Directors Playhouse]].
